title: SHF Data Center & AI Infrastructure Youth Development Pathway

DISCOVER.purpose: Build curiosity, infrastructure literacy, and systems thinking.

EXPLORE.purpose: Apply technical foundations through supervised labs and troubleshooting.

PREPARE_PROVE.purpose: Specialize, document evidence, and prepare for transition.

TRANSITION.purpose: Connect demonstrated learning to postsecondary and workforce options.

courses.title: Where Does the Internet Live?
courses.description: Introduces the physical systems behind websites, apps, cloud services, streaming, and AI.
learningOutcomes: Explain that digital services depend on physical computing infrastructure.
Identify servers, networking, electricity, cooling, and security as data-center systems.
Describe both opportunities and community questions related to data centers.
courses.majorProject: Build a labeled visual model of a data center.

courses.title: Inside the Infrastructure
courses.description: Explores how computing, networking, power, cooling, sensors, and security work together.
learningOutcomes: Describe how components and supporting systems work together.
Trace a simple connection from a device through a network to a server.
Use a safe classroom scenario to identify possible causes of a system failure.
courses.majorProject: Troubleshoot a low-risk classroom infrastructure model.

courses.title: Build a Better Data Center
courses.description: Uses design constraints to balance infrastructure reliability, sustainability, community impact, and opportunity.
learningOutcomes: Compare design choices involving energy, cooling, connectivity, land, and reliability.
Use evidence to explain a community benefit and a community concern.
Present a design that balances technical and community constraints.
courses.majorProject: Design a community-aware hypothetical data center.

courses.title: How Data Center Systems Work
courses.description: Builds supervised technical foundations in hardware, networking, electricity, cooling, and operations.
learningOutcomes: Identify major server components and explain their roles.
Use basic network, power, heat, and capacity concepts in a supervised lab.
Document observations using accurate technical vocabulary and safe procedures.
courses.majorProject: Build and document a basic non-hazardous technical system model.

courses.title: Operating Reliable Infrastructure
courses.description: Applies technical foundations to monitoring, maintenance, troubleshooting, documentation, and incident response.
learningOutcomes: Follow a supervised procedure to investigate a simulated infrastructure issue.
Explain redundancy, backup power, cooling, monitoring, and preventive maintenance.
Create a clear incident record that separates observations from assumptions.
courses.majorProject: Respond to a simulated infrastructure scenario and produce an incident report.

courses.title: Choose Your Infrastructure Path
courses.description: Introduces supervised specialization choices while preserving a shared infrastructure foundation.
learningOutcomes: Compare infrastructure specializations and select a supported area for deeper practice.
Plan and document a supervised project using appropriate evidence.
Connect a career interest to technical learning, education, and future credentials.
courses.majorProject: Complete a specialization project proposal and evidence plan.

courses.title: From Student to Infrastructure Professional
courses.description: Integrates infrastructure knowledge, community analysis, communication, safety, and transition planning.
learningOutcomes: Integrate computing, networking, power, cooling, security, sustainability, and community considerations.
Present a design or technical solution with evidence, constraints, and tradeoffs.
Create a grounded transition plan for further education, training, or supervised work-based learning.
courses.majorProject: Build Ohio's Next AI Data Center: a hypothetical, community-aware capstone.

courses.title: Grade 12 Infrastructure Operations
courses.description: A small common core and advanced Technical Operations reference slice for eligible Grade 12 learners.
learningOutcomes: Communicate technical decisions across infrastructure teams.
Analyze and document safe multi-system operations scenarios.
courses.majorProject: Stabilize and document a simulated multi-system service incident.

courses.title: Grade 12 Networking and Fiber
courses.description: Advanced Networking and Fiber practice for eligible learners using resilient, simulated network scenarios.
learningOutcomes: Interpret resilient network paths and performance evidence.
Plan safe simulated network changes and document cross-team handoffs.
courses.majorProject: Diagnose and stabilize a simulated resilient network incident.

courses.title: Grade 12 Electrical Infrastructure
courses.description: Advanced critical-power reasoning for eligible learners using synthetic, simulation-only electrical infrastructure scenarios.
learningOutcomes: Interpret simplified critical-power architectures and A/B dependencies.
Analyze synthetic capacity, redundancy, telemetry, and incident coordination evidence safely.
courses.majorProject: Analyze and coordinate a simulated critical power failure.

courses.title: Grade 12 Mechanical / HVAC Infrastructure
courses.description: Advanced thermal-capacity and cooling-reliability reasoning for eligible learners using synthetic, simulation-only infrastructure scenarios.
learningOutcomes: Interpret simplified cooling architectures, airflow relationships, and failure domains.
Analyze synthetic thermal capacity, telemetry, redundancy, maintenance state, and incident coordination safely.
courses.majorProject: Diagnose and coordinate a simulated cooling capacity incident.

courses.title: Grade 12 Cybersecurity / Physical Security
courses.description: Advanced defensive identity, access, physical-security, monitoring, and incident-coordination reasoning using synthetic simulations.
learningOutcomes: Analyze synthetic identity, access, and physical-security relationships.
Correlate defensive events, preserve uncertainty, and document safe authorized escalation.
courses.majorProject: Investigate and coordinate a simulated access-control incident.

courses.title: Grade 12 AI / Cloud Infrastructure
courses.description: Advanced infrastructure reasoning for multi-node compute, storage, capacity, reliability, and cross-domain dependencies using synthetic simulations.
learningOutcomes: Interpret multi-node compute, virtualization, storage, and workload-placement relationships.
Analyze synthetic capacity, bottleneck, reliability, observability, power, and cooling evidence safely.
courses.majorProject: Diagnose and stabilize a simulated AI compute cluster capacity incident.
futureCompetencyCandidates: AI infrastructure capacity and bottleneck analysis
distributed infrastructure reliability and incident coordination

transition.purpose: Use approved evidence and future partner pathways to support postsecondary or workforce decisions.

specializationTiming.decision: Grade 11 begins with a shared core, then students select a primary specialization; Grade 12 deepens that branch and integrates it into a collaborative capstone.
specializationTiming.primaryAssignmentRule: At most one ACTIVE PRIMARY specialization per learner, organization, and program; changes preserve transferred history.

grade12EligibilityPolicy.notReadiness: Grade 12 eligibility is educational progression status, not career readiness, credential status, licensure, or employment eligibility.

flexibility: A student may change a primary branch after an advising review and prerequisite check.
A secondary focus may be taken through approved cross-specialization electives.
Individual and team project formats must preserve equivalent learning outcomes.
Selection is a curriculum-planning decision, not an automated readiness score.

sharedGrade11Core.title: Safety and Professional Practice
sharedGrade11Core.whyCommon: Every infrastructure pathway needs safe boundaries, permissions, escalation, and reliable procedures.

sharedGrade11Core.title: Documentation and Technical Communication
sharedGrade11Core.whyCommon: Specialists must communicate observations, decisions, evidence, and handoffs to other teams.

sharedGrade11Core.title: Reliability and Systems Thinking
sharedGrade11Core.whyCommon: Infrastructure failures cross domain boundaries, so every learner needs shared reliability language.

sharedGrade11Core.title: Evidence, Feedback, and Portfolio Boundaries
sharedGrade11Core.whyCommon: Learners need to distinguish practice, artifacts, reviewed evidence, and future competency decisions.

sharedGrade11Core.title: Career and Transition Planning
sharedGrade11Core.whyCommon: Students should compare education, training, apprenticeship, and work-based learning options without being steered to one outcome.

specializations.title: Data Center Technical Operations
specializations.purpose: Deepen server, Linux, monitoring, deployment, troubleshooting, and operational procedure practice.

futureEvidenceCandidates.candidate: interpret monitoring data and document escalation

specializations.title: Networking and Fiber
specializations.purpose: Develop deeper understanding of switching, addressing, structured cabling, fiber, and connectivity troubleshooting.

credentialAlignments.ageAppropriateness: partner and equipment safety review required

specializations.title: Electrical Infrastructure
specializations.purpose: Build theory, diagram, monitoring, and safe low-voltage learning while reserving hazardous work for qualified partners.
safetyPrerequisites: qualified supervision for any physical equipment
no mains panels or energized power supplies
licensed/apprenticeship work belongs to external partners

specializations.title: Mechanical and HVAC Infrastructure
specializations.purpose: Develop thermal, airflow, environmental monitoring, and preventive-maintenance reasoning without unsupervised industrial service.
safetyPrerequisites: industrial HVAC service requires qualified supervision
no refrigerant, energized equipment, or mechanical service work

futureEvidenceCandidates.candidate: propose preventive checks for a model system

specializations.title: Cybersecurity and Physical Security
specializations.purpose: Apply defensive access, monitoring, permissions, and infrastructure-protection concepts in synthetic environments.
safetyPrerequisites: no credential theft, exploitation, persistence, or unauthorized scanning

specializations.title: AI and Cloud Infrastructure
specializations.purpose: Connect accelerators, virtualization, storage, networking, power, cooling, capacity, and reliability.

futureEvidenceCandidates.candidate: interpret an AI infrastructure power and cooling scenario

constructionDecision.reason: Construction and infrastructure delivery materially support every branch, but current evidence does not justify a separate full specialization.

prepareProveArchitecture.grade11ProjectModel: SPECIALIZATION PROJECT WITH COMMON SAFETY, DOCUMENTATION, AND REVIEW CRITERIA

grade12CapstoneModel.title: Build Ohio's Next AI Data Center
grade12CapstoneModel.model: COMMON COLLABORATIVE CAPSTONE WITH SPECIALIZATION ROLES AND INDIVIDUAL ACCESSIBLE EQUIVALENTS

grade12Architecture.courseAssignmentRelationship: Specialization assignment establishes branch identity; future Grade 12 course or lesson assignment remains a distinct curriculum participation fact.

advancedBranches.purpose: Apply multi-system operations, Linux, deployment, reliability, incident coordination, and runbook reasoning.
advancedBranches.safetyBoundary: simulation and authorized supervised operations; no production authority

advancedBranches.purpose: Analyze resilient network paths, performance, fiber documentation, and authorized network changes.
advancedBranches.safetyBoundary: authorized sandbox only; no unauthorized scanning or production changes

advancedBranches.purpose: Reason about critical power capacity, redundancy, monitoring, and professional escalation.
advancedBranches.complexity: synthetic critical-power incident and capacity scenarios
advancedBranches.safetyBoundary: simulation only; no energized systems, panels, switchgear, or professional service

advancedBranches.purpose: Analyze high-density thermal capacity, environmental telemetry, redundancy, and safe escalation.
advancedBranches.safetyBoundary: simulation only; no refrigerant, pressurized systems, energized equipment, or industrial service

advancedBranches.purpose: Coordinate defensive identity, access, physical-security, monitoring, and evidence-preservation decisions.
advancedBranches.complexity: correlated synthetic cyber and physical events
advancedBranches.safetyBoundary: authorized synthetic systems only; no offensive testing or physical-security bypass

advancedBranches.purpose: Analyze multi-node compute, capacity, data movement, reliability, power, cooling, and cost tradeoffs.
advancedBranches.complexity: synthetic multi-domain workload placement and failure scenarios
advancedBranches.safetyBoundary: simulation or disposable sandbox; no production cloud accounts, billing, or secrets

capstone.title: Build Ohio's Next AI Data Center
capstone.scenario: A fictional Ohio site with compute demand, network, power, cooling, security, reliability, sustainability, workforce, and community constraints.
capstone.teamRules: Roles may be duplicated or represented through integrated-mode work; no learner is blocked by cohort size or lack of a six-person team.
capstone.individualAttribution: Team membership never proves contribution; each individual result identifies learner-owned work and evidence.
capstone.review: One generic authorized competency decision record; optional feedback contributors do not bypass reviewer authority.
capstone.reassessment: New individual evidence or versioned team submission may receive a new review while preserving prior history.

capstoneEntryPolicy.notReadiness: Capstone entry is educational authorization, not program completion, credential status, career readiness, or employment eligibility.

ownership.projectDomainAudit: The repository has generic project-adjacent operational records but no canonical youth collaborative project/team submission domain suitable for activation; define the contract now and implement the smallest generic Project integration before executable capstone authoring.

competencies.advancedSpecializationCandidates: One or two reviewed candidates per branch, defined and activated in a later content phase.

completionContract.competencyRelation: Program completion and competency demonstration remain separate institutional facts.
completionContract.credentialRelation: No credential, license, apprenticeship hour, or certificate is issued by curriculum completion.
completionContract.readinessRelation: No career or employment readiness score is created.

events.decision: Do not add Grade 12-specific events until executable persistence is implemented.

assessmentOwns: assessment results under its existing contract
projectOwns: future project submission and review when canonical infrastructure exists
credentialOwns: future credential issuance by an authorized provider
careerOwns: canonical career identity and career facts
boundaries.competencyStatus: IMPLEMENTED: generic evidence and competency review foundation from Phase 16; Grade 11 content remains scoped
boundaries.credentialStatus: DEFERRED: planning and potential alignment only; nothing is issued
boundaries.employerStatus: DEFERRED: partner categories are planning references, not commitments
boundaries.privacyRule: Employer or partner context does not grant access to learner lessons, grades, assessments, portfolio, readiness, or evidence without explicit future authorization.

safety.rule: Classroom simulation and low-voltage learning are distinct from professional electrical or mechanical work.
